$comment: ts.device is 95 days old while ts.server is current - a gateway that was offline and has just reconnected. No live partition exists for this row, and none ever will: the record only gets older. DECIDED BEHAVIOUR - RetentionGuard SKIPS the write, increments records_expired_on_arrival{type}, logs at WARN and ACKs the delivery. It is NOT dead-lettered: the record is valid, the DLQ never expires anything, and a redrive would re-derive this same verdict forever. That is the redrive-age trap from the other end - a DLQ message redriven after ~90 days lands here and increments a counter, which is a no-op that looks like a recovery. This is deliberate data loss by a signed decision, which is why it is metered and alerted rather than silent.
